transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I can’t stop focusing on how one side of my face looks. It seems crooked and kind of swollen to me, especially when I see myself on lesson videos. Once I notice it, I feel like the students, parents, and other staff must be staring at that instead of listening to what I’m saying.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to cover it up, because of how you feel about that part of your face?

Yes. Before I post a recorded lesson or join a parent conference, I keep adjusting the camera angle and checking how my face looks. I’ll replay clips over and over, and sometimes I catch myself covering part of my face with my hand while I’m talking.

If it looks bad to me, I’ll re-record the whole thing, sometimes again and again. It takes up so much time that I miss prep work or end up late getting to my classes.
When you look at your face and feel something is wrong, does it feel like a real physical issue you need to fix, or do you feel anxious that others are judging you based on how you look?

It feels like both, I guess. When I see it on the lesson videos, that one side of my face looks crooked and swollen to me, like something is actually wrong with it. And then I can’t stop thinking that the students or parents or other staff are noticing it too, instead of paying attention to what I’m saying.
When you're worried about how your face looks, does the main concern feel like it's about the appearance itself, or more about how others are reacting to it?

It starts with the appearance itself. I see that one side of my face on the lesson videos and it looks crooked or swollen to me, and then I get stuck on it. After that, I start thinking everyone else must be seeing it too—students, parents, staff—and focusing on that instead of what I’m saying.

When you're looking at your face and feeling upset about how it looks, is it more that you feel something is physically wrong with your face, or more that you're worried others are judging you for it?

It’s more that it feels like something is physically wrong with my face first. I’ll see that one side looking crooked or swollen on the lesson videos, and I just can’t stop seeing it.

Then pretty quickly I start worrying that the students, parents, or other staff are staring at it instead of listening to what I’m saying.

When you're most upset about how your face looks, is it because you can't stand how the crooked or swollen part looks, even when no one else is watching, or is it more because you're worried about what others might think when they see you?

It’s mainly that I can’t stop seeing it myself first. On the lesson videos, that side of my face looks crooked and swollen to me, and once I notice it, I just get stuck on it.

Then it turns into thinking the students, parents, or staff must be staring at it too, instead of listening to what I’m saying.
When you're alone and not recording a lesson or interacting with others, do you still find yourself frequently checking or worrying about how that side of your face looks?

Yes. Even when I’m alone, I still end up checking it and thinking about it. It’s not only when I’m recording, though the lesson videos make it worse. Once I notice that side of my face looking crooked or swollen, I can’t really unsee it, and then I start thinking about how it must look to students or parents or other staff.

When you’re by yourself and not thinking about students or staff, is the main issue that you’re upset about how your face looks, or is it more that you imagine others would judge you if they saw it that way?

It’s mainly that I’m upset by how it looks to me. Like, when I see that crooked, swollen-looking side of my face, especially on the lesson videos, I just can’t stop focusing on it.

Even if I’m by myself, it bothers me first because it looks wrong to me. Then I start thinking, if it looks that obvious to me, students or parents or staff must be noticing it too.

When you look at that side of your face and it looks crooked or swollen to you, does it seem to you like the problem is that your face actually looks that way, or does it feel more like you're just overly sensitive to how it might appear to others?

It feels like it actually looks that way. I know maybe other people might not see it the same way, but when I watch the lesson videos, that side of my face looks crooked and swollen to me, and I can’t stop noticing it.

Then I start thinking the students, parents, or staff must be staring at it instead of listening to what I’m saying.

When you look at your face and see that side looking crooked or swollen, do you feel that your appearance is truly unacceptable or even ugly, or do you feel more that others will negatively judge you even if it doesn’t look that bad to you?

It feels like both, but it starts with me seeing it as really wrong. When I watch the lesson videos, that side of my face looks crooked and swollen, and I can’t stop focusing on it.

Then I start thinking the students, parents, and staff must be staring at that instead of listening to what I’m saying.

When you're most upset about how your face looks, is it mainly because you believe the crooked or swollen appearance is truly unacceptable, or is it more about the idea that others will think badly of you if they see you that way?

It’s mainly that I believe it really looks unacceptable when I see it. I can’t stop seeing that crooked, swollen-looking side of my face on the lesson videos, and once I notice it, I get stuck on it.

Then it turns into thinking the students, parents, and staff must be staring at that instead of listening to what I’m saying.

When you're by yourself and not interacting with anyone, does the main distress come from how bad the crooked or swollen part looks to you, or from imagining that others would judge you negatively if they saw it that way?

Even when I’m by myself, it starts with how bad it looks to me. Like, I’ll see that side of my face in the lesson videos and it looks crooked and swollen, and I just can’t stop focusing on it.

Then pretty quickly I start imagining the students or parents or staff noticing it too, like they’re staring at that instead of listening to me.

When you're most upset about how your face looks, is it mainly because you believe the crooked or swollen appearance is truly deformed or unacceptable in reality, or is it more about the idea that others will think badly of you if they see you that way?

It’s mainly because, when I see it, it looks really wrong to me. I keep noticing that crooked, swollen-looking side of my face in the lesson videos, and I can’t let it go.

Then I start thinking the students, parents, and staff must be staring at it instead of paying attention to what I’m saying.

When you’re most upset about how your face looks, would you say it’s mainly because you feel your face is actually deformed or unattractive, or is it more that you’re afraid others will judge you negatively for it?

Then I start thinking the students, parents, and staff must be staring at it instead of listening to what I’m saying.
